cleanIntro: The Accura MR-X and LR-X take down without tools: a lever releases the fore-stock, the barrel comes off the action, and the Quick Release Breech Plug unscrews with your fingers even after a long session. ⛔ How urgently you must clean depends on the barrel: plain stainless needs it the same day, a Nitride-treated one is far more forgiving — but the breech plug and firing pin never are.

steps.title: ⛔ Read the serial number FIRST — CVA recalled a range of in-lines
steps.action: Before you clean, load or fire anything, read the serial number off the gun and look at how it ENDS. In August 1997 CVA recalled every in-line with a serial ending -95 or -96, and no catalog listing can tell you whether yours is one of them — only the number stamped on your gun can. If it ends that way, stop here and call CVA. Do not clean it, do not load it, and do not let anyone else use it.
steps.aside: If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the rifle under any circumstances.
steps.quote: In August of 1997, CVA implemented a Voluntary Recall of all in-line rifle models with serial numbers ending in -95 or -96.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — VOLUNTARY RECALL

steps.title: Open it and look through from the BREECH end
steps.action: Pull the extended tang of the trigger guard rearward until the action unlocks, pivot the barrel forward, and take the breech plug out by hand. Then look down the barrel FROM THE BREECH END. ⛔ If you cannot see light through it, assume it is loaded and push the obstruction out with a range rod — do not assume it is fouling.
steps.aside: Use a range/cleaning ramrod of sufficient length to push the load or obstruction out of the barrel.
steps.quote: Verify that the rifle is unloaded by looking down the barrel from the breech end. If you cannot see light through the barrel you must assume it is loaded.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — GETTING STARTED

steps.title: Take-down lever out, fore-stock off
steps.action: Engage the take-down lever on the LOWER surface of the fore-stock and pull it outward — that releases the fore-stock — then draw the forend gently off the barrel. No screwdriver, which is the whole point of the design.
steps.aside: Then, gently pull the forend off of the barrel.
steps.quote: Engage the take-down lever located on the lower surface of the fore-stock and pull it outward, which will release the fore-stock from the barrel.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

steps.title: Breeching lever back, barrel off the action
steps.action: Pull the breeching lever rearward and open the action. With the fore-stock gone the barrel pivots forward and lifts off the action entirely.
steps.quote: Pull the breeching lever to the rear and open the action. With the fore-stock removed, the barrel will pivot forward and off of the action.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

steps.title: Breech plug out BY HAND, then set it soaking
steps.action: Turn the breech plug counter-clockwise by hand — CVA's Quick Release plug needs no tool even after dozens of shots. Wet it thoroughly with solvent and set it aside to soak while the bore is done.
steps.aside: Simply unscrew the breech plug with your fingers to remove.
steps.quote: Remove the breechplug by turning it counter clockwise by hand. No tool is needed. Wet the breechplug thoroughly with cleaning solvent and set aside.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

steps.title: Damp patches, brush, then patches until clean
steps.action: Jag on a rod, a patch or two damp with cleaning solvent (for Blackhorn 209) or water (for pelletised propellant) to take the bulk out. Then a properly fitting brush wet with solvent, several full-length strokes. Then damp patches, a minute or two to work, and dry ones after — repeat until it is clean.
steps.aside: Use a good quality non-petroleum gun oil to protect the bore.
steps.quote: Place a properly fitting brush on the rod and make several fulllength strokes through the barrel. The brush should be wet with solvent for this step.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

steps.title: Plug: threads, face, primer pocket, flash hole — then GREASE
steps.action: Wipe every surface of the soaked plug, threads included, and make certain the front, the primer pocket and the flash hole are clean. Cotton swabs for the corners. ⛔ Then apply breech plug grease or high-temperature anti-seize generously to the threads and install it FINGER TIGHT — over-tightening is what makes a plug impossible to remove later.
steps.aside: Generously apply breechplug grease or high temperature anti-seize to the breechplug threads and install into the barrel finger tight
steps.quote: Take the solvent-soaked breechplug and wipe all surfaces, including the threads, with patches or a rag.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

steps.title: Breech face and the action, then a rust preventative
steps.action: Solvent patch over the breech face and the action areas you can reach, cotton swabs for the rest, then wipe dry and put a rust preventative oil on.
steps.aside: Wipe dry with a clean patch or rag and apply a rust preventative oil.
steps.quote: Use a patch wet with solvent to scrub the breechface and other action areas that you can reach.
steps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

deepSteps.title: Firing pin bushing out — bushing, pin, spring, recess
deepSteps.action: With a properly fitting screwdriver take the firing pin bushing out of the front of the breech face; the pin and its spring drop out. Clean the parts AND the recess thoroughly with swabs, lubricate, and reinstall with a light coat of breech plug grease on the bushing threads.
deepSteps.aside: A light coating of breechplug grease on the bushing threads is advised.
deepSteps.quote: Using a properly fitting screwdriver remove the firing pin bushing from the front of the breechface. The firing pin and spring will drop out. Clean these parts and the firing pin recess thoroughly, lube and reinstall.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Accura MR-X / LR-X Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed in CLEANING YOUR CVA ACCURA RIFLE

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Damp patches first — solvent for Blackhorn 209, water for pellets
Brush wet with solvent, several full-length strokes
Damp patches, a minute to work, then dry patches until clean
Non-petroleum gun oil to protect the bore

cleaning.name: BREECH PLUG (Quick Release — no tool)
tasks: Soaked in solvent while the bore is done
⛔ Front face, primer pocket and flash hole clear
⛔ Threads greased, installed FINGER TIGHT only

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE & ACTION
tasks: Solvent patch and swabs, wiped dry, then rust preventative oil

cleaning.name: FIRING PIN ASSEMBLY
tasks: Bushing out; pin, spring and recess cleaned and lubricated
Light breech plug grease on the bushing threads

reassembly: Firing pin, spring and bushing back in, bushing threads lightly greased.
⛔ Breech plug threads greased with breech plug grease or high-temperature anti-seize, installed FINGER TIGHT.
Barrel back onto the action, breeching lever closed.
Fore-stock on and its take-down lever pushed back home.
Firing pin retraction checked, then a look through the bore from the breech.
fncheck: Reassembled: breech plug finger tight with greased threads, barrel back on the action, fore-stock clipped on by its take-down lever. Check the firing pin assembly works — trigger back, hammer pressed forward, and the pin must recess again when the hammer is released. Then look through the barrel from the breech end and confirm light before loading anything.
